title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Exhibition Hall on 1968-12-20

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1968 show featuring Pigpen’s classic “Turn On Your Lovelight” and Jerry’s acoustic jam on “Mountains of the Moon”, with modest hiss but overall good sound.
ai_review.review: The concert is remembered as a lively festival set where Pigpen shines on “Turn On Your Lovelight” and the band delivers an inspiring acoustic outro to “Mountains of the Moon”. Reviewers praise Jerry’s fluid solos and Phil’s solid bass work, while noting the recording has some background hiss but remains clear enough for enjoyment, especially after EQ tweaks. Overall the performance is rated highly and the soundboard source is considered good for its age.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong positive feedback on musical performance (many 5‑star reviews, standout songs) combined with generally good soundboard quality despite some hiss results in a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Instruments and vocals are loud but slightly muffled by background hiss; overall crisp for a 1968 board, with reviewers noting EQ can improve clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short but punchy Dead set within a larger festival, featuring classic Pigpen numbers and an acoustic jam to close, maintaining high energy throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Acoustic guitar jamming at the end of “Mountains of the Moon” and fluid solos up and down the neck were highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for playing “Mountains of the Moon” well, showing solid bass work.
